events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present THE HEROINES, a new exhibition by Seattle-based artist Victoria Haven. For this body of work, Victoria Haven referenced The Heroides, a collection of poems by Ovid written from the perspective of fifteen heroines of Greek and Roman mythology. Using the poems as source material and framework, the works in the exhibition dissect and reassemble mythological narratives into an invented language. The Heroines Alphabet, a series of graphite drawings, uses the title of the show as a system for revealing hidden words. Placed in a grid, Haven connects adjacent letters in ‘The Heroines’ to form new words, some with multiple readings or meanings. The Linguistic Architecture drawings abstract the alphabet further, transforming each letter of the title phrase into dark, inky rectangles with bright scarlet notations. Stripped of the actual letters, the words remain as only an echo of the informing system. The fifteen heroines are further revealed in a large-scale wall drawing with accompanying sound installation which layers incantatory murmurings taken from classical translations and a contemporary adaptation of Ovid’s epistolary poems. Ideas of language, voice, and story continue to unfold throughout the gallery in various forms, including silkscreen prints, mirrored objects, paintings, and a levitating, triangular bronze Penelope sculpture. Join us at the gallery Saturday, September 12th, at 2:30 pm for an artist talk with Victoria Haven and author Claire Dederer discussing the process surrounding this body of work and how it connects to ideas of perception, voice and language in her artist practice.
events.title: THE HEROINES · Victoria Haven

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Outside City Limits Forget the commute. Turn the car around! Leave civilization behind and delight in the fused-glass landscapes of Linda Gerrard and wander through the threaded tree paintings of Michelle L. Purvis instead. Michelle’s lifelong fascination with trees, mountains, and how they relate to humans strongly influences her art. In this series of framed acrylic paintings on paper, each work is a portrait of a specific tree, dressed in embroidered finery to fit its personality. She made their acquaintance and sketched them from life while she was camping or on vacation. While they may have been created completely in her studio, Linda’s fused-glass landscapes evoke a real sense of natural place. Starting with a base sheet of glass, she builds her images by arranging and kiln-firing layer after layer of colored glass, often leaving lovely textured details on the surface. Linda and Michelle, two long-time members of the gallery, invite you to take in the vistas of meadow, marsh and mountainside, to reach out to stroke the colorful bark of the trees or a heron’s plumage, and to discover what lies just Outside City Limits. Showing in the front windows of Alberta Street Gallery. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

Celebrate the artistic history of southwest Old Town and the newly dubbed Pink Light District in carnival style with performances, vendors, and revelry all along the six block stretch from the waterfront to Big Pink! Featuring vendors at the Saturday Market and along Ankeny, roving performances by some of Portland’s best circus, street performance, and musical artists, and Staycation specials at businesses throughout the Pink Light District, this three-day spectacle of food, festivities, and fun caps off with staggered Pink Light Processions - an all-ages community celebration reviving the “pilgrimages of pleasure seekers” of the 1920s with a family friendly twist! Join us on a joyous procession from the SW Waterfront to the Paris Theatre Patio in your favorite pink costume, craft project, or outfit - the bigger the better because you ARE the float for this rose colored revel filled with Portland-style whimsy and weird! Plus, be sure to grab one of our custom directory fliers and build your personal Pink Light itinerary: bring the whole family on a stroll through the Saturday Market, visit Voodoo Donuts, dip in to Dan and Louis for dinner, and treat your tastebuds at Black Cat Custard; or make it a daycation just for the adults with a meal at Mother’s, a drop by Dante’s for a dram, then catch a show at the Can Can and pop in for bite-sized burlesque at Madam Cooper’s Parlor. The choice is yours to mix and match with more than thirty iconic businesses, old and new, to choose from! Check out all of the Pink Light District businesses here: https://www.pinklightpdx.org/explore#business-list What To Expect: The Ankeny Alley Staycation Street Fair kicks off with discounts and specials on food, drink, and more at the neighborhood’s regular events and area businesses on Friday. Then we head into Portland Staycation weekend with two days of vendors, roaming performers, featured Ankeny Alley Stage performances, and the Pink Light Processions - community celebrations down southwest Ankeny filled with music, art, and whimsy! Created to bring together local business owners, the Association quickly grew into a community hub and the caretaking agency for the Ankeny Alley Plaza cultivating neighborhood arts, entertainment, and events in the plaza through support from the neighborhood's commercial and non-profit members. Stretching from West Burnside to Pine Street and from Naito Parkway to 6th Avenue, the Pink Light District brings together artists, businesses, venues, and neighbors to create a cleaner, safer, and more active downtown. Home to beloved landmarks including the Paris Theatre, Kit Kat Club, Voodoo Doughnut, Portland Saturday Market, the Waterfront Cherry Blossoms, and the city's iconic Big Pink tower, the district celebrates everything that makes Portland creative, quirky, and unforgettable. Expanded through a year of virtual gatherings, the exhibition reflects on how artistic dialogue continues to shape creative practice beyond the residency itself. Through photography, video, textiles, ceramics, painting, and installation, the artists explore migration, identity, memory, grief, ecology, ancestral knowledge, and care. Like beads threaded together, each work retains its individuality while contributing to a larger conversation about belonging, transformation, and the enduring connections forged through shared experience. events.summary: More than 40 leading local architecture firms present the best designs they hoped to build but that didn’t come to pass. Projects will include Allied Works’ elegant proposal commissioned by the New York Metropolitan Museum for its Modern and Contemporary Art Wing, West of West’s concept studies for infill housing in Los Angeles and Portland, Henneberry Eddy’s adaptive reuse of the recently destroyed Centennial Mills, and many more. In addition, the exhibition offers visions from Portland’s past, from Edward Bennett’s 1932 plan to reenvision Portland in the City Beautiful movement to Skidmore Owings Merrill’s “Delta Dome,” a 40,000-seat stadium in Delta Park, to GGN’s radical re-envisioning of Mt Tabor Park. It's a survey of Portland's past ambitions and its current array of design talent!
events.title: Unseen Portland Architecture: the best of Portland design. Never built

events.summary: PICA's celebrated Time-Based Art Festival is a time for us, as people, as Portlanders, as artists and art appreciators alike, to BE together. By immersing ourselves in performances, artist talks, installations, music, and community for five days, we coalesce to feel something, to spend time with art. TBA is a human experience. It is for people and by people, and it cannot be replicated. With TBA, we will show up to experience the moment, the tension, the beauty. And at a time when we can get lost in technology, critical global issues, and the mess of the day-to-day, taking a moment for you—for art—is a radical act. This September, for just five days, join us. Sit with artists as they generously and fearlessly present their work. Share a communal movement. Experience the art of our time. Tickets and passes are on sale now at pica.org/tba.

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour
events.title: Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness - Inaugural Concert Season

events.summary: Join us on September 12th for a special advance screening of Cai Indermaur’s award-winning documentary, The Pain And The Power, at Clinton Street Theater. Screening will be followed by a community conversation with the film’s subject Logan Lynn. Tickets on sale now at the Clinton Street Theater box office or at www.ThePainAndThePower.gay Presented by Grammy Award winning band Portugal. The Man’s KNIK Records / PortuGAY — About the Film — Decades after a sixteen-year addiction to cocaine, alcohol, and crack nearly ended his life, a Queer musician retraces his memory, music, and the wreckage left behind. The Pain and The Power is an award-winning, unflinching documentary portrait of artist, activist, and survivor Logan Lynn, by filmmaker Cai Indermaur. Tracing a 30-year career forged at the intersection of queerness, faith, addiction, trauma, and self-reinvention, and structured around the songs from Lynn’s latest record of the same name, the film treats music not as background but as a living character. Beginning in rural Nebraska and Texas inside a fundamentalist Christian world hostile to any type of difference, the film follows Lynn’s early sense of displacement, religious trauma, and abuse, and the ways secrecy and fear shaped both identity and survival. Through intimate interviews with Lynn, and decades of archival footage, music videos, and home movies, the film charts a restless trajectory: early success, underground acclaim, addiction, public collapse, and the slow, deliberate work of rebuilding a life on one’s own terms. Behind the scenes footage from early music videos, vintage tour clips, and present-day studio conversations collide with moments of humor, tenderness, and brutal honesty, and features stories about Lynn’s history with Elliott Smith, The Dandy Warhols, The Get Up Kids, 80s popstar Tiffany, his embattled relationship with Harvey Weinstein, and more. The result is neither a redemption arc nor a nostalgia piece, but a meditation on what it means to outlive the versions of yourself that no longer serve you. The Pain and The Power asks what remains after belief systems fail, relationships end, and the spotlight moves on; and how art can transform damage into something communal, generous, and alive. The film was named Best Documentary at the London Independent Film Awards (UK), Best Debut Documentary at the Athens International Monthly Art Film Festival (Greece), Best LGBTQ+ Feature at the Milan Indie Film Festival (Italy), Best Documentary and Best LGBTQ+ Film at the Global Visionaries Film Festival (Singapore), Best First-Time Director at the Berlin Indie Film Festival and the Portugal Indie Film Festival, and it won the Silver Award for Feature Documentary at the Paris Film Awards, the Milan Gold Awards, the London Movie Awards, and the Hollywood Gold Awards.
events.title: The Pain and The Power

events.summary: Written in 1936, this light-hearted comedy has relevance for today in addressing the main theme of finding one’s own way in today’s complex society, while lightly viewing such topics as distrust of government, domestic terrorism and fear of foreign conflicts. “Grandpa” Vanderhof (Robert Lovitz) once worked in the competitive business world. One day, he realized he was unhappy, so he stopped working. Since then, he spends his days catching and raising snakes, watching graduation ceremonies, visiting old friends, and doing whatever else he wants. His daughter Penny (Marilyn Stacey) writes plays simply because a few years ago a typewriter was delivered to the house by accident. His son-in-law Paul Sycamore (Todd Hermanson) spends hours in the basement making illegal fireworks and playing with erector sets. His granddaughter Essie (Bonnie Auguston) sells candy and has been clumsily attempting ballet for over eight years. His grandson-in-law Ed Carmichael (Aiden Brown) plays the xylophone (or tries to) and accidentally distributes Marxist propaganda. Joining this free-for-all are Rheba (Caren Graham), the household cook; her unemployed boyfriend, Donald (Shaun Hennessy); Essie’s opinionated Russian ballet instructor, Mr. Kolenkhov (Mark Schwahn); Olga (Trisha Todd), a Russian Grand Duchess; Gay Wellington (Adrienne Southard), a heavy-drinking actress; Wilbur C. Henderson (Douglas Hout), a forlorn IRS employee; and Mr. De Pinna (Danny Bruno), a deliveryman who arrived 8 years ago and decided to stay. He now helps with the fireworks and dresses in Roman togas to pose for Penny’s portraits. All is somewhat calm until three men from the government (Christopher Sparks, Dan Weiss, and Erik James) visit to investigate Ed’s flyers. In this crazy mix of characters, there is also Alice (Taylor Jean Grady), Penny and Paul’s other daughter and, apparently, the only “normal” family member. She met Tony Kirby (Noah Matthew Rich) at his dad’s Wall Street investment firm, and they’ve fallen in love. Culture shock and fireworks fly when Mr. Kirby (Jeremy Southard) and Mrs. Kirby (Wendy Martel) come to visit. But the message is clear: “Life’s pretty simple if you just relax,” as Grandpa puts it. You Can’t Take It With You is directed by Don Alder. Set design is by Chris Whitten, lighting design is by Demetri Pavlatos, costume design is by Janelle Sutton, prop design is by Allen R. Phillips, the stage manager is Alex Salem, the assistant stage manager is Nat Weinham, and the producer is Steve Knox.
events.title: You Can't Take It With You

events.summary: SEPTEMBER FLIGHT FEATURING 2 SOLOS BY Don Nigro September 11–27 Fri/Sat 7:30, Sun 2 $38 per person Imago Theatre, 17 SE 8th Avenue imagotheatre.com TICKETS https://onthestage.tickets/show/imago-theatre/6a56bc1797fd36b14c05ee83 Tickets also available at the door. Theatre opens one hour before showtime. All seats $38. The show is for mature audiences. The Dark, performed by Joe Cullen (Salomé, Design for Living) and Cincinnati, performed by Diane Slamp (Geography of a Horse Dreamer, Design for Living). Direction by Jerry Mouawad. THE DARK A man in his thirties grapples with a fundamental question: does he truly exist? This dilemma, first encountered at age four, drives the narrative of this ten-page script. Director Jerry Mouawad calls it "the perfect warm-up for Nigro’s work and his intriguing solos, many of which take place in a theatre." CINCINNATI "It’s hard not to feel that this piece was written specifically for Imago," says Slamp, who portrays a lost professor navigating a world of tragedy, sex, and philosophical diatribes. Her diversions reveal a desperate search for redemption amidst personal disaster. "Cincinnati is multi-layered, blending mythology and realism with an ontological examination of life and being," explains Mouawad. "It’s a gem for an audience seeking a new kind of theatre. Don’t let the heavy themes mislead you; this is a small spectacle with humor and high style. I see it as a consciousness tangling with forces of nature, an uncertain reality, and a triad of personas—real or unreal—in a lecture that pushes the boundaries of endurance.” Production Credits: *Light Design:* Ronnie Rantis Costume Design: Laura Helgeson Sound Design: Myrrh Larsen Note: For Mature Audiences In October, Imago returns with October Flight, featuring more solos by Don Nigro.
events.title: September Flight

events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Forged & Fired: Art by Flame Fire is one of humanity’s oldest tools for transformation. From forged steel and kiln-fired clay to molten silver and sculpted wax, heat is the catalyst that turns raw elements into striking fine art. Curated by Alberta Street Gallery member Leslie McMillan, this invitational exhibition features six artists—Larry Holt, Bobby Pedersen, Cindy Caufman, John Hyland, Diane Moskowitz, and Ann Coskey—who harness extreme temperatures to bend raw materials to their vision. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Outside City Limits Forget the commute. Turn the car around! Leave civilization behind and delight in the fused-glass landscapes of Linda Gerrard and wander through the threaded tree paintings of Michelle L. Purvis instead. Michelle’s lifelong fascination with trees, mountains, and how they relate to humans strongly influences her art. In this series of framed acrylic paintings on paper, each work is a portrait of a specific tree, dressed in embroidered finery to fit its personality. She made their acquaintance and sketched them from life while she was camping or on vacation. While they may have been created completely in her studio, Linda’s fused-glass landscapes evoke a real sense of natural place. Starting with a base sheet of glass, she builds her images by arranging and kiln-firing layer after layer of colored glass, often leaving lovely textured details on the surface. Linda and Michelle, two long-time members of the gallery, invite you to take in the vistas of meadow, marsh and mountainside, to reach out to stroke the colorful bark of the trees or a heron’s plumage, and to discover what lies just Outside City Limits. Showing in the front windows of Alberta Street Gallery. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Featuring vendors at the Saturday Market and along Ankeny, roving performances by some of Portland’s best circus, street performance, and musical artists, and Staycation specials at businesses throughout the Pink Light District, this three-day spectacle of food, festivities, and fun caps off with staggered Pink Light Processions - an all-ages community celebration reviving the “pilgrimages of pleasure seekers” of the 1920s with a family friendly twist! Join us on a joyous procession from the SW Waterfront to the Paris Theatre Patio in your favorite pink costume, craft project, or outfit - the bigger the better because you ARE the float for this rose colored revel filled with Portland-style whimsy and weird! Plus, be sure to grab one of our custom directory fliers and build your personal Pink Light itinerary: bring the whole family on a stroll through the Saturday Market, visit Voodoo Donuts, dip in to Dan and Louis for dinner, and treat your tastebuds at Black Cat Custard; or make it a daycation just for the adults with a meal at Mother’s, a drop by Dante’s for a dram, then catch a show at the Can Can and pop in for bite-sized burlesque at Madam Cooper’s Parlor. The choice is yours to mix and match with more than thirty iconic businesses, old and new, to choose from! Check out all of the Pink Light District businesses here: https://www.pinklightpdx.org/explore#business-list What To Expect: The Ankeny Alley Staycation Street Fair kicks off with discounts and specials on food, drink, and more at the neighborhood’s regular events and area businesses on Friday. Then we head into Portland Staycation weekend with two days of vendors, roaming performers, featured Ankeny Alley Stage performances, and the Pink Light Processions - community celebrations down southwest Ankeny filled with music, art, and whimsy! Created to bring together local business owners, the Association quickly grew into a community hub and the caretaking agency for the Ankeny Alley Plaza cultivating neighborhood arts, entertainment, and events in the plaza through support from the neighborhood's commercial and non-profit members. Stretching from West Burnside to Pine Street and from Naito Parkway to 6th Avenue, the Pink Light District brings together artists, businesses, venues, and neighbors to create a cleaner, safer, and more active downtown. Home to beloved landmarks including the Paris Theatre, Kit Kat Club, Voodoo Doughnut, Portland Saturday Market, the Waterfront Cherry Blossoms, and the city's iconic Big Pink tower, the district celebrates everything that makes Portland creative, quirky, and unforgettable. events.summary: Earthbody Presence + Aura Archive present a gathering of forest bathing & before/after aura photos on 9/13 from 1-4:30pm in nature. Join Earthbody Presence and Aura Archive on Sunday, 9/14 from 1pm - 4:30pm at Dabney State Park for a gathering of: ❊ forest bathing ❊ before & after aura photography ❊ tea ceremony ❊ personal reflection ❊ aura readings & shared connection What is forest bathing? Julie, our guide, will offer a series of accessible, mindful invitations while exploring the natural environment with care and appreciation. Each invitation is crafted to connect your senses to the sights, smells, and textures of nature. Spend intentional time in the forest and remember your belonging. Forest bathing, also called forest therapy, is inspired by the Japanese practice of shinrin-yoku. It is a guided experience that allows you to slow down while connecting with nature, community, and with yourself. What is aura photography? Aura photography is a tool to visually convey the current colors of your energy field. Aura archive’s aura camera technology uses bio-sensor hand plates to measure electrodermal activity (moisture, heat + the tiny currents in your hands that read the nervous system and emotional state). Then the color mapping tools within the device, communicate with a long-exposure camera to superimpose your specific color pallet on polaroid film. After your photograph develops, gorgeous colors will appear on the polaroid with a different signature based on your present state. The placement of colors, formation + location all carry significant, and specific meaning. Aura photography is usually accompanied by a color analysis, and intuitive reading for deeper awareness into your unique energetic blueprint - at this moment in time... to be archived. About Your Guides: Julie Jansen (she/her), Certified Forest Therapy Guide with Earthbody Presence Julie is a meditation practitioner, movement educator, and a certified Forest Therapy Guide. Since childhood she has found awe, tranquility, and a sense of homecoming in nature and through somatic movement. Julie guides individuals and groups in meditation, movement, and land-based practices to connect people with tools that help them remember their wholeness. Her gentle, trauma-informed guidance empowers individuals to bring presence-based practices into their lives as they encounter the struggles and joys of being human. Julie lives and works on the ancestral homeland of the Upper Chinook tribe in what is now Portland, Oregon. Julie is a certified Forest Therapy Guide with The Association of Nature and Forest Therapy. She also holds a Mindfulness Teacher Certification from Inward Bound Mindfulness Education, a Masters of Art in Art Education, and she completed a 200-hour yoga teacher training through The Yoga Space in Portland, Oregon. Currently, she teaches meditation and movement at Portland State University along with facilitating Earthbody Presence offerings. Chel (she/they), Aura Photographer + Intutive Aura Reader with Aura Archive Chel is a venusian projector and Joy Guide. she is anAura Photographer and Intuitive energy Reader. Chel is a seer and guide into the liminal as a Reiki Master/teacher, Past Life Regressionist, Hypnotherapist, Psychedelic Guide, and a death doula - for those in the flesh, and a death doula to this dying system, as we shift into the new earth. She is a community organizer and space holder; both on a 1:1 basis and in groups. She has a vast background in the non-profit sector of hospice care and mental health services, as well as Children’s theater, stand up comedy, poetry writing and communing with the trees. Her passion lies in guiding others to heal and uncover authentic joy through self-expression, self-reflection and play. She believes micro and macro transformation is possible when we are living in reverence to one another and the earth, as we align with our personal internal compass, and embodying our divine truth from a heart-led space. Chel believes aura photography is a wonderful tool for people to receive a visual representation of their truest essence. events.summary: Written in 1936, this light-hearted comedy has relevance for today in addressing the main theme of finding one’s own way in today’s complex society, while lightly viewing such topics as distrust of government, domestic terrorism and fear of foreign conflicts. “Grandpa” Vanderhof (Robert Lovitz) once worked in the competitive business world. One day, he realized he was unhappy, so he stopped working. Since then, he spends his days catching and raising snakes, watching graduation ceremonies, visiting old friends, and doing whatever else he wants. His daughter Penny (Marilyn Stacey) writes plays simply because a few years ago a typewriter was delivered to the house by accident. His son-in-law Paul Sycamore (Todd Hermanson) spends hours in the basement making illegal fireworks and playing with erector sets. His granddaughter Essie (Bonnie Auguston) sells candy and has been clumsily attempting ballet for over eight years. His grandson-in-law Ed Carmichael (Aiden Brown) plays the xylophone (or tries to) and accidentally distributes Marxist propaganda. Joining this free-for-all are Rheba (Caren Graham), the household cook; her unemployed boyfriend, Donald (Shaun Hennessy); Essie’s opinionated Russian ballet instructor, Mr. Kolenkhov (Mark Schwahn); Olga (Trisha Todd), a Russian Grand Duchess; Gay Wellington (Adrienne Southard), a heavy-drinking actress; Wilbur C. Henderson (Douglas Hout), a forlorn IRS employee; and Mr. De Pinna (Danny Bruno), a deliveryman who arrived 8 years ago and decided to stay. He now helps with the fireworks and dresses in Roman togas to pose for Penny’s portraits. All is somewhat calm until three men from the government (Christopher Sparks, Dan Weiss, and Erik James) visit to investigate Ed’s flyers. In this crazy mix of characters, there is also Alice (Taylor Jean Grady), Penny and Paul’s other daughter and, apparently, the only “normal” family member. She met Tony Kirby (Noah Matthew Rich) at his dad’s Wall Street investment firm, and they’ve fallen in love. Culture shock and fireworks fly when Mr. Kirby (Jeremy Southard) and Mrs. Kirby (Wendy Martel) come to visit. But the message is clear: “Life’s pretty simple if you just relax,” as Grandpa puts it. You Can’t Take It With You is directed by Don Alder. Set design is by Chris Whitten, lighting design is by Demetri Pavlatos, costume design is by Janelle Sutton, prop design is by Allen R. Phillips, the stage manager is Alex Salem, the assistant stage manager is Nat Weinham, and the producer is Steve Knox.
events.title: You Can't Take It With You

events.summary: SEPTEMBER FLIGHT FEATURING 2 SOLOS BY Don Nigro September 11–27 Fri/Sat 7:30, Sun 2 $38 per person Imago Theatre, 17 SE 8th Avenue imagotheatre.com TICKETS https://onthestage.tickets/show/imago-theatre/6a56bc1797fd36b14c05ee83 Tickets also available at the door. Theatre opens one hour before showtime. All seats $38. The show is for mature audiences. The Dark, performed by Joe Cullen (Salomé, Design for Living) and Cincinnati, performed by Diane Slamp (Geography of a Horse Dreamer, Design for Living). Direction by Jerry Mouawad. THE DARK A man in his thirties grapples with a fundamental question: does he truly exist? This dilemma, first encountered at age four, drives the narrative of this ten-page script. Director Jerry Mouawad calls it "the perfect warm-up for Nigro’s work and his intriguing solos, many of which take place in a theatre." CINCINNATI "It’s hard not to feel that this piece was written specifically for Imago," says Slamp, who portrays a lost professor navigating a world of tragedy, sex, and philosophical diatribes. Her diversions reveal a desperate search for redemption amidst personal disaster. "Cincinnati is multi-layered, blending mythology and realism with an ontological examination of life and being," explains Mouawad. "It’s a gem for an audience seeking a new kind of theatre. Don’t let the heavy themes mislead you; this is a small spectacle with humor and high style. I see it as a consciousness tangling with forces of nature, an uncertain reality, and a triad of personas—real or unreal—in a lecture that pushes the boundaries of endurance.” Production Credits: *Light Design:* Ronnie Rantis Costume Design: Laura Helgeson Sound Design: Myrrh Larsen Note: For Mature Audiences In October, Imago returns with October Flight, featuring more solos by Don Nigro.

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour
events.title: Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness - Inaugural Concert Season

THE EXPERIENCE We welcome back local filmmaker and producer Barbara Bernstein and her film Chasing Chimeras: The Lure of Deceptive Climate Solutions, which tells the stories of people living in the crosshairs of the fossil fuel industry's self-serving climate solutions, including renewable diesel, hydrogen, renewable natural gas, biofuels, carbon capture and storage, and carbon offsets. Following the film, Barbara will lead a discussion. ON SCREEN: Chasing Chimeras: The Lure of Deceptive Climate Solutions 2025. Directed by Barbara Bernstein. Runtime: 55 minutes. As we confront the existential crisis of climate chaos, there are two paths we can take. We can make dramatic changes that meaningfully reduce carbon emissions, or we can accept the fossil fuel industry's self-serving climate solutions-renewable diesel, hydrogen, renewable natural gas, biofuels, carbon capture and storage, and carbon offsets. Chasing Chimeras: The Lure of Deceptive Climate Solutions tells stories of people living in the crosshairs of these proposals, working to expose the dangers that these projects pose to their lives, homes, communities, and the planet. In contrast to fossil fuel industry solutions, the documentary examines the need to implement verified and trusted renewable energy sources \(wind, solar, and geothermal\), energy conservation, and nature-based carbon capture and storage solutions that take advantage of natural carbon sinks such as old growth forests and wetlands. ON STAGE: Barbara Bernstein \(Director\) - ProducerBarbara Bernsteinis a musician, composer, performance artist, radio producer and filmmaker. Besides her recent documentaries "Chasing Chimeras" and "Once a Braided River," her award-winning radio documentaries, internationally broadcast on public radio stations, include two pieces about the struggle to stop the Pacific Northwest from becoming a fossil fuel export hub: Holding the Thin Green Line and Sacrifice Zones; Sculpted By Fire \(the role of fire in shaping western forests and sustaining healthy forest ecosystems\); Salmonlands \(the cultural significance of diminishing salmon runs in the Northwest\) and Rivers That Were \(the industrialization of the Colorado and Columbia Rivers\). She is currently working on a new documentary about liberating the culverted creeks that flow under Portland's Industrial sacrifice zone along the Willamette River. events.summary:
Code & Coffee is an inclusive, informal co-working session: drink your beverage of choice, bring your laptop, and hang out with your peers! Have engaging conversations, or focus on work or projects. This is a great opportunity to learn from others, share your knowledge, and possibly collaborate on side projects, online courses, or even your day-to-day work.

---- Schedule ----

You're welcome to drop in anytime during the event. We understand that everyone may have external commitments and challenges - join us when you can!

We have informal unscheduled introductions - practice your personal elevator pitch, or take things slower to build your confidence.

---- Venue ----

Fly Chai allow us to informally and freely use their space. If within your budget, we'd appreciate your help to sustain our use of the venue, by purchasing something tasty, whether Chai or otherwise.

Find us at tables with a Code&Coffee sign - or a clump of laptop-users!

Wifi and power outlets are available.
Our meeting area should be accessible - please let us know if not.

---- What to expect ----

Smaller events than you may be used to, with a mixed crowd week-to-week. We expect this is likely due to us meeting weekly, at a less central location.

These may result in what you're looking for:
    A smaller, less intimidating, lower pressure, cozy atmosphere.
    A mix of regular and new faces.
    A simpler schedule - every week, same time, same place - that you can drop into when you like.
    Being closer to you than other events.

Whether those are generally or partly to your liking, we hope you'll consider dropping by sometime!

---- Getting to the venue ----

Look for the venue on the meetup Google map, or alternatives like OpenStreetMap.

-- Driving --

There are limited parking spaces on a lot outside the venue (4+1 accessible), with more in the surrounding area.

-- Transit options --

Beaverton Central (Red/Blue MAX), then walk~ 8 minutes

Beaverton Transit Center (Red/Blue MAX, bus, WES) then walk ~11 minutes

For a shorter walk to the venue, take a bus from Beaverton Transit Center (52 to Farmington/Hall, 76 to Watson/Broadway, 57 to Canyon/Watson)

events.summary: This summer, Portland Japanese Garden is host to a glowing world of light. Guests who visit the Calvin and Mayho Tanabe Gallery will see that through carefully hand-woven and sculpted washi (Japanese handmade paper made from plant fibers), soft light and shadow inspire a magical sense of place, evoking the unique environment of the Pacific Northwest. events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Forged & Fired: Art by Flame Fire is one of humanity’s oldest tools for transformation. From forged steel and kiln-fired clay to molten silver and sculpted wax, heat is the catalyst that turns raw elements into striking fine art. Curated by Alberta Street Gallery member Leslie McMillan, this invitational exhibition features six artists—Larry Holt, Bobby Pedersen, Cindy Caufman, John Hyland, Diane Moskowitz, and Ann Coskey—who harness extreme temperatures to bend raw materials to their vision. Exhibited in Lavaun's Community Gallery. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.
events.title: Forged & Fired: Art by Flame

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Outside City Limits Forget the commute. Turn the car around! Leave civilization behind and delight in the fused-glass landscapes of Linda Gerrard and wander through the threaded tree paintings of Michelle L. Purvis instead. Michelle’s lifelong fascination with trees, mountains, and how they relate to humans strongly influences her art. In this series of framed acrylic paintings on paper, each work is a portrait of a specific tree, dressed in embroidered finery to fit its personality. She made their acquaintance and sketched them from life while she was camping or on vacation. While they may have been created completely in her studio, Linda’s fused-glass landscapes evoke a real sense of natural place. Starting with a base sheet of glass, she builds her images by arranging and kiln-firing layer after layer of colored glass, often leaving lovely textured details on the surface. Linda and Michelle, two long-time members of the gallery, invite you to take in the vistas of meadow, marsh and mountainside, to reach out to stroke the colorful bark of the trees or a heron’s plumage, and to discover what lies just Outside City Limits. Showing in the front windows of Alberta Street Gallery. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: Being “in scene” is where storytelling comes alive on the page. It’s where readers feel, understand, and enter a story’s world—where we experience deeper emotional truths that keep us turning pages. Scene is the foundation of memorable storytelling, and it is a craft that crosses every genre. This five-day intensive teaches writers the essential elements of compelling scene construction. Over five class meetings, students will learn to create authentic characters, ground readers in vivid and purposeful setting, weave exposition seamlessly into narrative, and build scenes that draw readers in and hold them page after page. In each session we move from craft principle to practice and feedback, so that each writer leaves understanding how scene works and having practiced, too. What Writers Will Learn Character & Setting Craft: • Ground story in vivid, purposeful locations • Create characters with clear motivation and authentic behavior • Develop compelling dialogue that reveals character Pacing & Structure: • Build tension through countervailing forces • Drive momentum with action and conflict • Practice page-turning pacing techniques Voice & Subtext: • Weave in distinctive narrative voice • Add depth through subtext and implication • Balance showing and telling for maximum impact Daily Structure Each session will include: • Study of effective published scenes across genres • Analysis exercises mapping scene and expository techniques • Supportive read-alouds of new work • Collaborative workshopping of three participants’ pieces • Q&A on scene craft and technique Access Program We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. events.summary: The oeuvre of Tennessee Williams expands far beyond his well-known plays. His prolific dedication to writing resulted in experimental one acts, collections of poetry, song lyrics, essays, a memoir, several short story collections, & two novels. This seminar will focus on his fiction. Beginning with his novel The Roman Spring of Mrs. Stone \(1950\), we’ll explore how his prose developed from more straightforward language to experiments with disordered time & stream of consciousness—powerfully applied in Moise and the World of Reason \(1975\). Bridging these two novels are his many short stories, which range from the brutally realist to the sensationally surreal. events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present THE HEROINES, a new exhibition by Seattle-based artist Victoria Haven. For this body of work, Victoria Haven referenced The Heroides, a collection of poems by Ovid written from the perspective of fifteen heroines of Greek and Roman mythology. Using the poems as source material and framework, the works in the exhibition dissect and reassemble mythological narratives into an invented language. The Heroines Alphabet, a series of graphite drawings, uses the title of the show as a system for revealing hidden words. Placed in a grid, Haven connects adjacent letters in ‘The Heroines’ to form new words, some with multiple readings or meanings. The Linguistic Architecture drawings abstract the alphabet further, transforming each letter of the title phrase into dark, inky rectangles with bright scarlet notations. Stripped of the actual letters, the words remain as only an echo of the informing system. The fifteen heroines are further revealed in a large-scale wall drawing with accompanying sound installation which layers incantatory murmurings taken from classical translations and a contemporary adaptation of Ovid’s epistolary poems. Ideas of language, voice, and story continue to unfold throughout the gallery in various forms, including silkscreen prints, mirrored objects, paintings, and a levitating, triangular bronze Penelope sculpture. Join us at the gallery Saturday, September 12th, at 2:30 pm for an artist talk with Victoria Haven and author Claire Dederer discussing the process surrounding this body of work and how it connects to ideas of perception, voice and language in her artist practice.
events.title: THE HEROINES · Victoria Haven

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Outside City Limits Forget the commute. Turn the car around! Leave civilization behind and delight in the fused-glass landscapes of Linda Gerrard and wander through the threaded tree paintings of Michelle L. Purvis instead. Michelle’s lifelong fascination with trees, mountains, and how they relate to humans strongly influences her art. In this series of framed acrylic paintings on paper, each work is a portrait of a specific tree, dressed in embroidered finery to fit its personality. She made their acquaintance and sketched them from life while she was camping or on vacation. While they may have been created completely in her studio, Linda’s fused-glass landscapes evoke a real sense of natural place. Starting with a base sheet of glass, she builds her images by arranging and kiln-firing layer after layer of colored glass, often leaving lovely textured details on the surface. Linda and Michelle, two long-time members of the gallery, invite you to take in the vistas of meadow, marsh and mountainside, to reach out to stroke the colorful bark of the trees or a heron’s plumage, and to discover what lies just Outside City Limits. events.summary: El Grito Portland is the premier Latiné cultural and arts celebration in the Pacific Northwest, serving as a vibrant tribute to the independence of Mexico and several Latin American nations including Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Chile, and Belize. Held annually on Sep 15 and 16 at the Rose Quarter Commons, this free festival honors rich traditions and indigenous roots through an authentic showcase of heritage.The festival's cultural offerings include: Music and Dance: Attendees can experience live performances by mariachi bands, folkloric ballet dancers, Aztec dancers, and various Latin American musical groups. Art and Handcrafted Goods: The "Poderosas Pavilion" is a dedicated market featuring local Latina artisans and indigenous artists who showcase and sell handcrafted items such as traditional embroidery, jewelry, and apothecary products. Culinary Traditions: The event features a wide range of authentic Mexican cuisine and traditional dishes from local vendors, along with refreshing drinks and Mexican-inspired Northwest beer. Traditional Ceremonies: A central highlight is the official "Ceremony of El Grito," a powerful reenactment of the 1810 civic call for independence led by the Mexican Consul.

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour

events.summary: Join us for an evening with Aiden Thomas at the Q Center to celebrate the launch of Cemetery Boys: Espiritu! Aiden will be in-conversation with Tehlor Kay Mejia about the book, followed by an audience Q&A, and then a book signing line and photo opportunity. We will have copies of all of Aiden's books for sale at the event, with the option to preorder at the link provided during the RSVP checkout. Please note: This event will be taking place at the Q Center located at 4115 N Mississippi Ave, Portland, OR 97217 *New York Times*\-bestselling author Aiden Thomas returns to the beloved world of *Cemetery Boys*, this time following Julian—chaos magnet extraordinaire. With restless spirits vanishing and a dark demon from their past emerging, he and Yadriel might be the only ones reckless enough to stop a threat that could tear their world apart. Julian used to be a ghost and now he can’t stop seeing them. Ever since Julian was sacrificed as part of a forbidden ritual, he has been able to see and talk with spirits. And that’s really cool, since it allows him to be part of his new boyfriend's community. But Julian’s seeing other things, too: flickers at the edge of his vision, eyes burning in the night, and “dark spots” on people—gaping wounds that thrum and bleed shadow. Yadriel has never heard of anything like it, either, and he’s so busy with his new brujx responsibilities that Julian hates for his problems to ruin what little time they have together. Then a strange new brujx shows up. Angel, as a nonbinary bruje, can heal the living and release the dead, but more than that, they can also see the same dark spots as Julian. Despite Yadriel’s reservations, Julian eagerly accepts their help. But, Angel’s ruthless methods feel wrong to Julian. With the shadows growing darker and the discovery of a gaping dark spot on his friend Luca, Julian has to decide who he wants to put his trust in, and just how far he’s willing to go to save what is his. Aiden Thomas is a trans, Latinx, New York Times Bestselling Author with an MFA in Creative Writing from Mills College. Originally from Oakland, California, they now make their home in the Pacific NW. Aiden is notorious for not being able to guess the endings of books and movies, and organizes their bookshelves by color. Their books include the Sunbearer Duology, Cemetery Boys, and Lost in the Never Woods. Tehlor Mejia (he/him) is a bestselling and award winning author of queer books for all ages. His debut young adult novel, We Set the Dark on Fire, received six starred reviews, as well as the Oregon Spirit Book Award for debut fiction, and the Neukom Institute Literary Arts Award runner up honor for debut speculative fiction. It was featured on Seventeen, Cosmopolitan, and O by Oprah Magazine’s best books lists, and was a 2019 book of the year selection by Kirkus and School Library Journal. The sequel, We Unleash the Merciless Storm, followed to continuing acclaim. In 2020 he released a co-write, Miss Meteor, with fellow queer Latinx author Anna-Marie McLemore. His recently concluded second YA duology, Lucha of the Night Forest and Lucha of the Forgotten Spring, released from the Make Me a World imprint headed by Christopher Meyers. They have received multiple starred reviews, as well as the former receiving an International Latino Book Award in the Young Adult Fantasy and Adventure category. Tehlor was also thrilled to contribute to the beloved Addams Family franchise when he novelized the hit Netflix show Wednesday, that title was released from Random House Children’s Books in 2024. His fifth offering in the young adult space, Marrow, a dark academia story starring a trans main character, is forthcoming from Wednesday Books in 2027. Across their varied body of work, Tehlor strives to create stories which showcase the importance of community, radical inclusion, and abolitionist values. He lives with his child, wife, and two dogs in his home state of Oregon, and is active on Instagram and Bluesky @tehlormejia.

events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present THE HEROINES, a new exhibition by Seattle-based artist Victoria Haven. For this body of work, Victoria Haven referenced The Heroides, a collection of poems by Ovid written from the perspective of fifteen heroines of Greek and Roman mythology. Using the poems as source material and framework, the works in the exhibition dissect and reassemble mythological narratives into an invented language. The Heroines Alphabet, a series of graphite drawings, uses the title of the show as a system for revealing hidden words. Placed in a grid, Haven connects adjacent letters in ‘The Heroines’ to form new words, some with multiple readings or meanings. The Linguistic Architecture drawings abstract the alphabet further, transforming each letter of the title phrase into dark, inky rectangles with bright scarlet notations. Stripped of the actual letters, the words remain as only an echo of the informing system. The fifteen heroines are further revealed in a large-scale wall drawing with accompanying sound installation which layers incantatory murmurings taken from classical translations and a contemporary adaptation of Ovid’s epistolary poems. Ideas of language, voice, and story continue to unfold throughout the gallery in various forms, including silkscreen prints, mirrored objects, paintings, and a levitating, triangular bronze Penelope sculpture. Join us at the gallery Saturday, September 12th, at 2:30 pm for an artist talk with Victoria Haven and author Claire Dederer discussing the process surrounding this body of work and how it connects to ideas of perception, voice and language in her artist practice.
events.title: THE HEROINES · Victoria Haven

It also houses an historic library and research center. Built in 1913, the station handled passenger and light freight service into 1929. After that only light freight came through. Burlingham and Sons purchased the building as office space for their seed company. Unfortunately, over the years this building has gone through some internal and external changes but some of the original station remains and can easy be found. events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Forged & Fired: Art by Flame Fire is one of humanity’s oldest tools for transformation. From forged steel and kiln-fired clay to molten silver and sculpted wax, heat is the catalyst that turns raw elements into striking fine art. Curated by Alberta Street Gallery member Leslie McMillan, this invitational exhibition features six artists—Larry Holt, Bobby Pedersen, Cindy Caufman, John Hyland, Diane Moskowitz, and Ann Coskey—who harness extreme temperatures to bend raw materials to their vision. Exhibited in Lavaun's Community Gallery. Alberta Street Gallery is a cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: Last Thursday Artist Reception August 27, 6 to 9pm. Show Dates: August 27 through September 21. Outside City Limits Forget the commute. Turn the car around! Leave civilization behind and delight in the fused-glass landscapes of Linda Gerrard and wander through the threaded tree paintings of Michelle L. Purvis instead. Michelle’s lifelong fascination with trees, mountains, and how they relate to humans strongly influences her art. In this series of framed acrylic paintings on paper, each work is a portrait of a specific tree, dressed in embroidered finery to fit its personality. She made their acquaintance and sketched them from life while she was camping or on vacation. While they may have been created completely in her studio, Linda’s fused-glass landscapes evoke a real sense of natural place. Starting with a base sheet of glass, she builds her images by arranging and kiln-firing layer after layer of colored glass, often leaving lovely textured details on the surface. Linda and Michelle, two long-time members of the gallery, invite you to take in the vistas of meadow, marsh and mountainside, to reach out to stroke the colorful bark of the trees or a heron’s plumage, and to discover what lies just Outside City Limits. events.summary: Stringing Beads / Ensartar Cuentas brings together the work of Orquidia Violeta, Mariela Finvarb, Beatriz Bellorín, and Marisol Valencia in an exhibition that grew from the relationships formed during and after the 2024 Stelo Summer Invitational Residency. Expanded through a year of virtual gatherings, the exhibition reflects on how artistic dialogue continues to shape creative practice beyond the residency itself. Through photography, video, textiles, ceramics, painting, and installation, the artists explore migration, identity, memory, grief, ecology, ancestral knowledge, and care. events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. events.summary:
For September, we're taking advantage of a speaker in town for DevOpsDaysPDX, and making it an all-observability night, with FluentBit and OpenTelemetry.

Date: Wednesday, September 16, 2026
Time: 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM
Location: SteepleJack Brewing, Fireside Room, 2400 NE Broadway, Portland

Talks are typically recorded (opt-in by speakers)

A big thank you to SuSE for sponsoring catering at SteepleJack, as well as Eric's travel.

First Presentation: No C, No Opaque AI: Watch Your First Fluent Bit Contribution Happen Live

Speaker: Eric D. Schabell, SuSE

Contributing to a CNCF graduated project feels out of reach until someone shows you exactly how it happens. In this session, that someone is on stage doing it in real time — spotting a gap between what the Fluent Bit codebase actually does and what the docs say, opening a branch on a live fork, running the project's prose linter, writing a properly signed commit, and pushing a pull request that closes a real tracked issue. Every step, no shortcuts, no slides pretending to be a terminal.

You will leave knowing the two-repo mental model that makes Fluent Bit doc contributions work, the git habits that signal credibility to maintainers, and the AI guardrails that keep your name attached to work you actually stand behind. Your first PR does not require deep C knowledge. It requires knowing where to look, how to show your work, and when to keep your hands on the wheel."

Second Presentation: Devs, Transform (Your Data) and Roll Out!: Learning and Leveraging OTTL

Speaker: Reese Lee, New Relic

The OpenTelemetry Collector is OTel’s power tool for ingesting and processing your app and infrastructure data, but there’s even more you can do with your data before it reaches your backend! Learn how to start leveraging OTTL, or OpenTelemetry Transformation Language, to manage your data volume and quality. We’ll explore the syntax basics and its underlying architecture within the Collector, where its strength really comes into play, when to use it (or not!), and more.
events.title: Cloud Native PDX September: Observability Night!
